title: "Research"

My research is centered on **explainable AI**, **mechanistic interpretability**, **uncertainty quantification**, and **language-model reliability**.

## Research agenda

I am interested in explanations as operational signals: not only as post-hoc descriptions for humans, but as measurable quantities that can improve AI systems.

Current directions:

- detecting contextual hallucinations in retrieval-augmented generation,
- using model-internal features for evaluation and reliability,
- controllable generation with masked diffusion language models,
- explanation-based covariate drift detection,
- interpretable NLP systems for information extraction and document understanding,
- reliable AI workflows for science and industry.

## PhD thesis

**Beyond Human Interaction: Alternative Applications for Explanations** (TU Berlin / DFKI, since 2023)

Traditional XAI produces explanations for humans to read. My thesis instead treats attribution methods (Integrated Gradients, ALTI, LRP, and mechanistic decompositions of the residual stream) as internal signals that an AI system can consume itself. It is organised around three questions:

1. **Can explanations detect when the input distribution changes?** Attribution patterns shift before performance drops, enabling label-free drift detection.
2. **Can explanations improve retrieval in RAG systems?** Token-level attribution for pairwise embedding similarity, and attribution-based reranking of retrieved documents.
3. **Can explanations verify factuality?** Tracking which source tokens influence each generated token to detect contextual hallucinations and attach citations.

## Explainability as an engineering signal

A recurring theme in my work is that explanations can be used to **improve** AI systems, not only to explain them after the fact. This includes model monitoring, drift detection, model evaluation, and mechanistic diagnostics.

## Software Campus

**Software Campus Fellow / Project Lead — XPO**  
Industry partner: **Celonis**

I lead XPO, a 12-month project on explainability-guided prompt optimization and repair for reliable agentic workflows, with an emphasis on language-model reliability, grounding, and mechanistic diagnostics.

## DFKI projects

- **GenKI4Media** (2025–present) — transparency, traceability, and accuracy of AI-generated editorial content.
- **Data4Transparency** (2023–2024) — information extraction over leaked document collections for investigative journalists (OCCRP).
- **Green-AI Hub Mittelstand** (2024) — LLM entity linking for automated product carbon footprint estimation.
- **PLASS** (2020–2022) — information extraction and drift detection for supply-chain risk monitoring.

See [Projects](projects.qmd) for details.

## Collaboration interests

I am especially interested in source-grounded AI-for-science settings where model outputs should be constrained by provided evidence:

- mathematical or scientific reasoning,
- engineering and technical documentation,
- policy, legal, and financial reports,
- enterprise process and operational documents.
